newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto husband, province governor detained.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto husband, province governor detained.

text.p: Asif Ali Zardari, the husband of sacked Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, and Punjab province governor Raja Saroop Khan, were taken into custody by army officers on Tuesday, witnesses said.
They said the two men had been taken to an undisclosed place from the governor's house in the provincial capital Lahore.
Zardari, who had been investment minister in Bhutto's cabinet, was staying with Saroop Khan, a retired army general, at Governor House in Lahore, the witnesses said.
There was no immediate information on the reason for their detention, which followed President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of Bhutto's government on charges of corruption and misrule.
Leghari also dissolved the lower house of parliament and ordered fresh elections for February 3 to be supervised by a caretaker prime minister, Meraj Khalid.

On Monday, Saroop Khan summoned a session of the Punjab assembly for November 14 to vote on the political fate of provincial Chief Minister Manzoor Ahmad Wattoo, who was restored to his office by a court on Sunday.
